question: A pituitary macroadenoma compressing the optic chiasm classically produces a bitemporal (heteronymous) hemianopia because the crossing nasal fibres from both eyes are interrupted at the chiasm.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Nasal retinal fibres — which carry temporal visual field information — decussate at the chiasm. A pituitary tumour compressing the chiasm from below disrupts both sets of crossing fibres, producing bitemporal hemianopia.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The optic chiasm carries nasal retinal fibres (carrying temporal visual field) from both eyes; a central chiasmal lesion interrupts these crossing fibres, producing bitemporal field loss — the classic 'blinker' defect.
